description: Platform-agnostic base for all Docent platform schemas: the top-level envelope plus the cross-platform $defs (no platform-specific fields or wording). Composed by scripts/build-schemas.js with optional intermediate family layers (e.g. desktop.shared.schema.json) and a per-surface leaf delta into each published platform schema. Not used directly for validation — use the platform-specific schemas.

docent_format.description: Self-describing format stamp identifying which Docent platform and schema version produced this file. Lets any consumer pick the correct schema and route migrations without guessing. The platform and schema_version values are fixed (const) per published schema.

platform.description: The Docent platform that produced this file (set per published schema).

schema_version.description: The schema version this file conforms to (set per published schema).

steps.description: All step version records for this recording. Contains full history including re-recorded and deleted versions.

narration.description: Free-text narration describing the step intent. Present in narration mode.

narration_source.description: How the narration was provided. Written at capture alongside narration; the pairing is not schema-enforced.

step_type.description: Step classification in simple mode. Present in simple mode.

expect.description: Assertion type for validation steps. Present when step_type is 'validation'.

x.description: Pointer X at the action, in the capture surface's coordinate space: the capturing document's viewport (the document's layout pixels) for in-page capture, or the screen (physical pixels) for native capture.

y.description: Pointer Y at the action, in the capture surface's coordinate space: the capturing document's viewport (the document's layout pixels) for in-page capture, or the screen (physical pixels) for native capture.

modifiers.description: The modifier keys held when this action happened. Absent in a recording made before the field existed.

held_keys.description: The keys that were down when this action happened, other than the modifiers and other than this action's own key: each a key whose own key-down is a `key` action of this recording (its press, or the first key-down of it that was recorded when the press was not), named as that action names it, in the order they went down. Empty when no such key was known to be down, which is not the same as no key being down: a key whose key-down was not recorded is not named. Absent in a recording made before the field existed.

value.description: The entered value; the session-format document states each platform's cut. Sensitive values are masked at capture — passwords, payment fields designated by their autocomplete tokens, and fields whose name/id matches the shared financial/secret/SSN pattern — and the element is flagged redacted.
Visible text of the selected option; the session-format document states each platform's source.

key.description: What the press means on the active keyboard layout, named by the W3C UI Events `key` values (a, A, ?, Enter, ArrowUp), a space written as Space. The session-format document states the whole rule under Key names.

repeat.description: Whether key repeat generated this press: true for a press generated while the key was held down, false for the press itself. Absent where the capture layer does not record it; the session-format document states which do.

code.description: The physical key that was pressed, named by the W3C UI Events `code` values (KeyA, Minus, NumpadEnter, etc.): the key's place on the keyboard, the same whatever the active keyboard layout makes of the key. Absent where the press had no physical key the capture layer could name, and in a recording made before the field existed.

input_method_open.description: Whether an input method (the system's own entry of composed text, as for Japanese, Chinese or Korean) was on for the control that held the keyboard focus, as read at the press, before the key took effect. Absent where the capture layer did not read it; the session-format document states which do, and when.

input_method_conversion_mode.description: The input method's conversion mode as the platform gave it at the press, before the key took effect: a set of bits the session-format document states. Written only beside `input_method_open`; absent where it was not read.

source_element.description: The dragged element. Null when no drag start was observed for it: a drag begun before recording, or one whose start the capturing side did not observe.

element.description: The scrolled element. Null for a page-level scroll; the session-format document states each platform's source.

scroll_top.description: Vertical scroll offset of the scrolled container (the page when element is null) when the gesture settled: the container's offset in the document's layout pixels for in-page capture; 0 for native capture today, which observes wheel input rather than container offsets; the session-format document states each platform's source.

scroll_left.description: Horizontal scroll offset of the scrolled container (the page when element is null) when the gesture settled: the container's offset in the document's layout pixels for in-page capture; 0 for native capture today, which observes wheel input rather than container offsets; the session-format document states each platform's source.

delta_y.description: Net vertical displacement of the settled scroll sequence: the change in the scrolled container's vertical offset (in the document's layout pixels) for in-page capture, or the sum of the sequence's raw vertical wheel deltas as reported by the platform's input layer (native wheel-delta units, not pixels; sign follows the platform's wheel convention) for native capture; the session-format document states each platform's measurement and its anchor.

delta_x.description: Net horizontal displacement of the settled scroll sequence: the change in the scrolled container's horizontal offset (in the document's layout pixels) for in-page capture, or the sum of the sequence's raw horizontal wheel deltas as reported by the platform's input layer (native wheel-delta units, not pixels; sign follows the platform's wheel convention) for native capture; the session-format document states each platform's measurement and its anchor.

source.description: Identifies the switched-to context in the producing platform's own terms: a location or a process name (a process identifier stands in where the name cannot be read).

title.description: The switched-to context's title, or null when it has none.

opener_context_id.description: The context_id of the context that opened this one, or null when none is known or the producing platform records no opener.

source.description: Identifies the opened context in the producing platform's own terms: a location or a process name (a process identifier stands in where the name cannot be read), or null when unknown at open time.

window_closing.description: Whether closing this context closed its whole window; always true where every context is a window.

tag.description: Element kind or control type (e.g. a button, text input, or link). "unknown" when the element could not be identified.

id.description: Stable, developer-assigned identifier for the element. Null when absent.

name.description: Element name or accessible name. Null when absent.

role.description: Accessibility role of the element. Null when absent.

type.description: Element subtype when applicable, e.g. "password" for masked text inputs. Null otherwise.

autocomplete.description: The field's autocomplete hint when present (e.g. "cc-number"), used to identify sensitive payment fields. Null when absent or not applicable.

position_in_set.description: One-based position of the element within the logical set of related items it belongs to, as reported by the source accessibility layer. The logical set can differ from what is currently rendered. Null or absent when not reported.

size_of_set.description: Number of items in the logical set of related items this element belongs to (the counterpart of position_in_set), as reported by the source accessibility layer. Null or absent when not reported.

level.description: One-based depth of the element within a hierarchical set (e.g. an item's depth in a tree), as reported by the source accessibility layer. Null or absent when not reported.

framework_id.description: Identifier of the UI framework that supplies this element, as reported by the source accessibility layer. Applications can mix frameworks, so this is recorded per element. Null or absent when not reported.

language.description: The language the application declares for this element, as the application states it (a language tag such as "da" or "en-GB"; an application can state any string, the empty one included). Taken from the nearest element at or above this one that declares a language; the session-format document states each source. Null or absent when none declares one. A declaration, not a measurement of the text shown.

text.description: Visible text, truncated to 100 characters (a truncation mark may be appended); the session-format document states each platform's source and whether it marks the cut. Null for sensitive fields (password fields, and fields the shared sensitivity detection recognises) or when empty.

selector.description: Locator for the element: a platform-specific selector or accessibility path, or "coord:x,y" when only coordinates are available.

redacted.description: True when the captured value and/or text was redacted because the field was sensitive (a password, payment, or other PII field). Absent when nothing was redacted.

locators.description: Locator candidates: observed facts about how this element could be addressed at capture time. Each entry is a per-strategy shape; the set of valid strategies is platform-specific (see this schema's locator definition). Entries appear in the fixed order their strategy definitions are declared in the locator definition — that order is a serialization convention and carries no preference or ranking. Omitted when no candidates were observed; candidates whose value was empty are omitted rather than included empty.

described_after_ms.description: Milliseconds between the action's timestamp and the moment this element description (including any locator match measurements) was captured, as observed by the capture layer. 0 means the element was described at the input itself. Larger values mean the description reflects the interface as it stood that long after the input — the action's effects may already have run. Null or absent when not observed.

locator_match_count.description: How many elements this candidate matched, measured under the scope, order, and timing stated by this schema's locator definition. Present only where it was cheap to measure at capture time; absent means not measured, never a guess — though the current producers also write no pair for a candidate measured and matching nothing, the case the format encodes as match_index null with no match_count.

locator_match_index.description: Zero-based position of the acted-on element in this candidate's match list, measured together with match_count (0 <= match_index < match_count; the upper bound is stated here because it cannot be schema-enforced). Null means this candidate did not match the acted-on element at all (the current producers write it only beside a match_count). Absent means not measured — or, from the current producers, measured and matching nothing, as match_count states.

locator_masked.description: True when this candidate's value derived from sensitive content and was masked in place (the same mask glyph as other captured values); the entry is kept, never omitted. match_count and match_index were measured against the real value before masking. Absent when nothing was masked.

alt_graph.description: Whether AltGr was held at the action, as the system held it: the session format's Modifiers section states when a held AltGr key is not AltGr to the system. Absent in a recording made before the field existed.

context_id.description: Identifier for the window, tab, or surface in which the action occurred. Session-scoped; not persistent across restarts.

preferred_languages.description: The user's ordered language preference that applications are offered, most preferred first, as language tags (for example "da-DK"). Recorded context beside the action, never part of it; the session-format document states each source. Null when it could not be read.

metadata.description: User-defined key-value pairs. Values can be a string or an array of strings.
